summary: Milestone 6 (Communicative Purpose Framework) end-to-end acceptance PASSED against the public URL (https://dev-converse.preview.emergentagent.com). Backend: 8/8 pytest passes in /app/backend/tests/test_milestone6_communicative_purpose.py (initial run 7/8 in 277s with one test-script bug in _assert_common_shape — asserted 'exactly 1 ai turn' which is only true on the first /interact; fixed helper to check 'last turn is ai and ai_count == student_count == interactions_count', re-ran multi-turn test standalone in 111s = PASS). Coverage: (a) theory.communicative_purpose.primary populated correctly across 4 canonical purposes — persuasive (primary=persuade, secondary=[argue]), explanatory (primary=explain, secondary=[inform]), narrative (primary=narrate, secondary=[reflect]), analytical (primary=analyze, secondary=[interpret]); (b) mixed-purpose ('explain how algorithms work AND argue whether they should be regulated') yields BOTH explain AND argue across primary+secondary (primary=argue, secondary=[explain]) — holds multiple purposes, does not collapse to one; (c) purpose-adaptive teaching — narrative draft was NOT pushed a persuasive thesis (no forbidden 'thesis statement', 'state your argument', 'make a claim' phrasing) and NO rigid-template phrasing ('five-paragraph', 'three body paragraphs', 'topic sentence/evidence/analysis', 'hook-background-thesis') appeared on ANY draft; (d) M5A regression: intervention.focus=='writing' on every ordinary draft (all 4 single-purpose tests + all 3 multi-turn turns) and intervention.writing_not_content_check is non-empty in every case; (e) M1-M5 regression: multi-turn writing->revise->answer preserved theory_history v1..v3 with prior versions intact, currently_relevant_domains stayed at 2 across turns 1 and 2, all turns completed under 120s (no 502), no stage/grade/level language leaked; the revision correctly produced a `consolidate` intervention (recognize->name->use loop working); (f) session CRUD + PATCH telos still work. Frontend: 6/6 UI checks passed against the public URL — (i) `?dev` auto-creates preset session, lands directly in Student Workspace with writing-area visible (no Teacher Setup needed); (ii) typing a draft into writing-area + clicking continue-button produces an ai-invitation in the thread within ~30s; (iii) Dev Panel opens via open-dev-panel-button and communicative-purpose-block renders primary=persuade with inferred_from and uncertainty populated; (iv) intervention block shows focus + writing-not-content check fields; (v) new-test-session-button resets to a fresh empty workspace (writing-area cleared, ai-invitation gone); (vi) normal Teacher Setup flow still works — form renders, begin-session-button submits with all 3 required fields, quick-test-start-button link also starts a session. Screenshots captured showing purpose block populated, workspace-with-invitation, and empty-after-reset states.

minor.issue: Still returns 200 (not 201) for resource creation. Carried over from every prior iteration; tests assert 200; not blocking.

The prior iteration_10 flake (~1-in-10 empty-done frames from ingress-edge buffering) did not recur across 8 SSE calls in the M6 run. The single-retry wrapper `sse_interact_with_retry` in the new test file guards against it defensively; if it ever fires, both attempts count against the ~180s timeout.

issues: Secondary field renders as em-dash '—' when the LLM returns secondary=[] (e.g., simple persuasive draft). Correct visually — no fix needed — just noting that in the mixed-purpose backend test the same LLM did return secondary=['explain (how algorithms rank posts)'], so the UI will render both cases correctly. No action item.

action_items: None blocking. Milestone 6 acceptance holds end-to-end. Communicative purpose is correctly inferred across persuade/explain/narrate/analyze/interpret/reflect; mixed-purpose assignments genuinely hold both purposes (primary + secondary) rather than collapsing; purpose-adaptive teaching works (narrative not pushed to persuasive thesis; no rigid templates anywhere); M5A boundary (focus='writing', writing_not_content_check) preserved; theory_history v1..vN preserved across multi-turn; frontend Dev Panel purpose block + ?dev bypass + new-test-session-button + quick-test-start-button all render and function.

Optional (carry-over from iteration_10): return 201 from POST /api/sessions; loosen stale prompt-size assertions in test_developmental_engine.py (26KB) and test_milestone3_thesis.py (median 16KB) if they still tickle when STAGE-A picks two enriched domains.

Same pattern could be back-ported to test_milestone5_instruction_layer.py and milestone5a_boundary_eval.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py — CommunicativePurpose model (lines 124-131) and DevelopmentalTheory.communicative_purpose field (line 137) are correctly wired. The Pydantic default_factory=CommunicativePurpose gives every new session a clean empty purpose object; the LLM JSON output schema at line 314 spells out primary/secondary/inferred_from/uncertainty; and _compact_theory (line 367) surfaces communicative_purpose.model_dump() into the per-turn prompt so multi-turn reasoning can reference and refine it. Zero risk of KeyError; observed the field populate correctly on every one of ~8 live turns.

server.py — COMMUNICATIVE PURPOSE FRAMEWORK block in SYSTEM_MESSAGE (lines 264-269) is crisp: (i) it lists 10 canonical purposes as FUNCTIONS not genres, (ii) it explicitly permits (and requires) mixed-purpose holding, (iii) it says 'ask how well the writing accomplishes its communicative purpose — NEVER how closely it resembles a standard essay', (iv) it names writing concepts as function-shifting (thesis/introductions/organization/evidence/paragraphs/transitions/conclusions/counterargument/reader awareness/revision), (v) it explicitly frames functional patterns (Claim->Reasons->Support, Question->Process->Explanation, events-over-time, Observation->Interpretation->Support, Experience->Meaning->Insight) as PATTERNS NOT TEMPLATES. Empirically the guidance held on all four canonical purposes and on the mixed-purpose assignment.

server.py — Purpose-adaptive teaching held even in an edge case: when the ?dev preset (assignment='Argue whether social media improves or harms teen friendships.') was combined with a draft on the WRONG topic (school uniforms), the AI correctly (a) inferred primary=persuade from the ASSIGNMENT (not from the mismatched draft), (b) recorded the mismatch in communicative_purpose.uncertainty, and (c) redirected the student to write a sentence stating what they want the reader to accept about the ASSIGNED topic — a writing-function redirect, not a content prescription. This is a nontrivial coordination of M6 (purpose from assignment) + M5A (writing-not-content) + inside-outside coordination.

server.py — On the multi-turn regression the AI correctly moved from `instruct_then_invite` (turn 1: student announced a topic without an argument) -> `consolidate` (turn 2: student produced a real revision with position + reason) -> `invite_only` (turn 3: student explained their move). This is the intended Recognize -> Name -> Understand -> Use -> Reflect cycle from the DEVELOPMENTAL INSTRUCTION LAYER (lines 294-302), and it happened without any prompting from the test.

server.py — one subtle observation: _apply_engine_result snapshots the PRIOR theory into theory_history BEFORE replacing it (line 488-494). This means theory_history[N-1] holds the theory state that PRODUCED turn N, not the state after. My assertion in TestMultiTurnRegression correctly reflects this (v1 is pre-turn-1 empty; v2 preserves post-turn-1 domains, etc.). Semantics are correct; may be worth a one-line docstring on the field to make the ordering explicit for future readers.

frontend/src/App.js — the ?dev bypass path (lines 27-38) has one small quirk: if the browser ALREADY has a session id in localStorage, the ?dev query is ignored and the existing session is loaded. This is correct for developer convenience but means testers must clear localStorage OR click 'New Test' to actually see the ?dev preset kick in. The 'New Test' button (handleNewSession -> localStorage.removeItem + handleQuickStart) resolves this; documented behavior. No action needed.

frontend/src/components/DevelopmentPanel.jsx — communicative-purpose-block (lines 177-200) renders primary in amber, secondary as a bulleted List (with the shared List component's em-dash fallback for empty lists), inferred_from as text, and uncertainty ONLY when populated. This mirrors the backend field ordering cleanly and gracefully handles both single-purpose and mixed-purpose cases. Verified live.

TEST-SCRIPT BUG FIX: my initial _assert_common_shape helper had `assert len(ai_turns) == 1` which is only true on the first /interact of a session. Fixed to `assert last_turn.role == 'ai' and len(ai) == len(student) == len(interactions)`. Not a production defect — just a test-file bug I introduced and immediately fixed.

rca of the issue: No functional defect observed. Two minor process notes: (1) TEST-SCRIPT BUG (self-introduced, self-fixed): my _assert_common_shape helper asserted `len(ai_turns) == 1` which passes on the first /interact but fails on subsequent turns because ai turns accumulate in session.turns. Reproduction: any test that calls sse_interact_with_retry twice on the same session and then calls _assert_common_shape. Mitigation: replaced with `assert turns[-1].role == 'ai' and ai_count == student_count == interactions_count` which correctly encodes 'this /interact appended exactly one student + one ai turn'. Re-verified passing on the multi-turn test standalone. (2) The Dev Panel's Communicative Purpose block correctly renders on ?dev even when the assignment is 'social media harms teen friendships' but the student pastes an off-topic 'uniforms' draft — the AI infers primary=persuade from the ASSIGNMENT (correct), records the topic mismatch in communicative_purpose.uncertainty (also correct), and redirects the student to write about the assigned topic via a writing-function question rather than supplying content. This demonstrates purpose inference is driven by assignment first, then draft — the intended M6 behavior.
